text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says he objects to any Israeli changes to the status of Jerusalem that would affect the outcome of final status Middle East peace talks.
- Pre-election fever hits in the lawyers union, with four candidates to stand for post of head of the union in a hotly contested election.
- Israel appoints a new ambassador to Jordan.
- Industry minister says that Arabs are serious about implementing a common free trade zone to boost inter-Arab economic ties.
- Crown Prince Hassan, during a meeting with a member of the Spanish parliament, calls for action to confront the fear of Islam in the West.
- Jordanian prisoners in Israeli jails plan to strike in protest against their continued detention.
- Prosecutor refuses to release on bail the mayor of Zarqa who was jailed for calling deputies liars.

- King says the thorny issue of Jerusalem affects the future of peace and "that it should be discussed in the right time and framework..any changes in the holy city would abort the efforts towards consolidating mutual trust between Arabs and Israelis".
